title: Cumulus Compute - Redwood partner intro
next_steps: Redwood to send partner one-pager and pricing matrix by 2026-03-05
Schedule technical deep-dive with Jonah + Tom for 2026-03-10
Share SOC2/ISO security pack and KMS integration notes by 2026-03-06
action_items: Nina Patel - Send partner overview + pricing spreadsheet - 2026-03-05
Jonah Reed - Schedule and run technical deep-dive and benchmarking plan - 2026-03-10
Tom Wu - Share Cumulus infra topology and perf targets - 2026-03-06
summary: Intro/discovery between Redwood AE/SE and Cumulus Compute partnerships team. Discussed partner integration models (marketplace listing, co-sell, private deployments), technical constraints (VPC, KMS, GPU types), and next steps to run a pilot and security review.
topics: technical compatibility: H100/A100, KV cache, batching
transcript:
[00:00] Nina (Redwood): hey everyone thanks for making time, i'm nina from redwood inference, i'm the ae on this, with me is jonah our solutions eng. quick sound check?
[00:15] Rajiv (Cumulus): yep hearing you ok, rajiv here, lena and tom with me. great to meet you both.
[00:28] Jonah (Redwood): hey team, quick agenda — partner intro, high level GTM, then technical constraints and POC idea, then next steps. hope that works?
[00:36] Lena (Cumulus): works for us. we're looking at partners for inference stack — marketplace + private deployment options are interesting.
[00:45] Nina: perfect. quick context on redwood — we're a developer-first inference platform, we run hosted API and also dedicated and private options for vendors like you to resell or integrate. (mumble) we focus on predictable latency/cost, rollout controls, and observability.
[01:05] Rajiv: quick question — do you have a partner program? like referral vs reseller? and is there any channel co-sell?
[01:15] Nina: yes, we have a partner program; high-level options are marketplace listing + referral, co-sell for strategic partners, and private deployments where partners bundle a managed private control plane. we can send the partner one-pager after this.
[01:28] Tom: from a technical angle, what does private deployment look like — is it a VPC-connected control plane or on-prem image? our customers sometimes require air-gapped.
[01:38] Jonah: we support both. Redwood Private can be VPC with customer-managed networking and KMS integration; we also provide an on-prem package for regulated customers. note: the private control plane still needs a management plane that you can host — or we can host with strict tenancy.
[01:55] Lena: KMS — do you integrate with HSMs? customers ask for HSM/KMS for key separation.
[02:02] Jonah: yes, we integrate with cloud KMS providers and HSMs (bring-your-own-KMS), and you can configure key policies. audit logs and per-token traceability are supported.
[02:15] Rajiv: great. concurrency/throughput — what GPU types do you support? H100? A100? and what's the perf story for 8k/32k seq lengths?
[02:28] Jonah: we run on common GPU families — A100, H100, and have kernel selection for model architecture. for long sequences, we do KV cache management and chunked attention in the runtime. real numbers depend on model + quantization; for example on H100 with 8-bit quant we see 2-5x cost reductions and good latencies for 4k windows. we can run a bench on a representative model.
[02:50] Tom: do you do quantized floats like int8 or gptq style? we've seen accuracy regressions with some quant methods.
[02:59] Jonah: we support per-model quant profiles — int8, 4-bit QAT/LLM.int4-style and some GPTQ workflows; we include recommended profiles in Redwood Optimize. we also monitor quality and can rollback if regressions appear.
[03:14] Nina: quick commercial note — hosted is usage-based; dedicated and private have reserved contracts. partners often start with joint pilots on hosted then scale to dedicated.
[03:25] Lena: good to know. on security — our enterprise customers care about SOC2, ISO, SSO/SAML, RBAC. do you have certs and SSO integrations?
[03:35] Jonah: we have SOC2 Type II and are pursuing ISO; SSO with SAML/OIDC is supported, RBAC, and audit logs. i can share the security pack with compliance docs.
[03:46] Rajiv: nice. one concern is data residency — do you have region restrictions? we operate in eu and us, some APAC customers too.
[03:55] Nina: yes region-aware routing is supported; customers can pin regions and we can do private deployments in specific cloud regions.
[04:06] Tom: curious about SDK and integration effort — is this a single REST/SDK integration for both hosted and private?
[04:12] Jonah: yes same API and SDK primitives across modes; the idea is consistent interface so app teams don't change code when you move from hosted to dedicated. occasional config differences for auth and networking.
[04:24] Lena: from partnership GTM — we want to understand go-to-market: do you provide co-marketing funds, enablement kits, sales training?
[04:33] Nina: we have partner enablement docs, joint case studies, and for strategic partners we do co-marketing and lead sharing. we'll share a partner deck.
[04:42] Rajiv: on the POC — our preferred flow is run a benchmarking pilot with 1-2 enterprise customers, validate latency/cost, and then list on marketplace. is that typical?
[04:52] Nina: absolutely. typical path: discovery -> technical deep-dive -> pilot with performance benchmark -> security review -> marketplace/reseller agreement.
[05:03] Jonah: for the pilot we'd propose: 1) define 1-2 representative models and workloads, 2) run bench on both hosted and a dedicated setup, 3) collect latency/cost metrics and quality evals using your prompt set. we can do a 2-3 week pilot.
[05:20] Tom: sounds good. instrumenting quality metrics is key — can you hook into our eval harness? we use an internal eval pipeline.
[05:28] Jonah: yes we have tracing hooks and can export logs/metrics; we can also provide token-level breakdowns in the Console and export traces.
[05:36] Rajiv: about pricing — partners need predictable margins. is pricing list-based or negotiable? and for resell do you do partner discounts?
[05:46] Nina: pricing varies by tier; partners get partner pricing for resale programs. we'll include a sample pricing matrix; for dedicated/private it's negotiated based on commit.
[05:55] Lena: any known integrations with ISVs or SI partners we should be aware of? references help sell.
[06:02] Nina: we work with a number of cloud and SI partners — we can share a partner reference list (some names: Aurora GPU infra, Velascale).
[06:10] Tom: technical question — does Redwood support model routing/fallbacks? e.g., route to cheaper quantized variant if capacity constrained.
[06:18] Jonah: yes smart routing is a core feature; you can configure policy-based routing by latency/cost/region, with automated fallback to compatible variants.
[06:27] Rajiv: what about caching and prefix reuse? many of our customers want token-level caching to reduce costs for chat applications.
[06:36] Jonah: we support KV/prefix caching and continuous batching; Redwood Optimize suggests batching/caching settings per workload.
[06:44] Nina: just flagging, some of the partner use cases involve offering a managed private runtime to end customers — would Cumulus want Redwood to white-label or be a backend?
[06:55] Rajiv: ideally backend with co-branding. we want to own the customer relationship where possible.
[07:02] Nina: that's feasible — private deployments with partner-managed tenancy are common. commercial terms vary.
[07:10] Lena: onboarding friction: what's the expected time to onboard a partner and first pilot?
[07:17] Jonah: for a basic pilot on hosted — 1-2 weeks for config and test data; for dedicated/private it can be 4-8 weeks depending on infra and network requirements.
[07:27] Tom: do you provide terraform or helm charts for private installs?
[07:32] Jonah: we provide deployment manifests and infra-as-code templates; specifics depend on whether it's air-gapped.
[07:39] Rajiv: can we get a sample SLA for dedicated? our enterprise buyers will push on uptime and SLOs.
[07:46] Nina: yes we'll include sample SLAs in the partner pack. dedicated has SLA-backed uptime and latency targets.
[07:54] Lena: any regulatory constraints — e.g., FedRAMP or DPA? some of our Gov customers ask for FedRAMP.
[08:01] Jonah: we do not currently have FedRAMP; we can discuss roadmap but it's not out of box. we do have DPA support and data processing agreements for EU customers.
[08:12] Tom: for benchmarking, can we test both H100-confs and more cost-optimized GPU types, and compare quant profiles?
[08:20] Jonah: yes — we can run benches across instance types and quant levels. we'll propose a bench plan in the follow-up.
[08:28] Rajiv: i'll flag internal success metrics: margin > 20% on resell, latency P50 < 120ms for typical chat use, and support for per-tenant isolation.
[08:39] Nina: good metrics. we'll aim to design the pilot to capture those.
[08:45] Marta (Cumulus): quick commercial — channel registration process? we need partner agreement templates.
[08:52] Nina: we'll send partner agreement templates and an MSA skeleton.
[08:57] [09:00] -- brief pause, small cross-talk --
[09:12] Jonah: quick technical note — sequence lengths and model families will change kernel selection; for LLaMA/OPT style models we have specific kernels, for transformer variants it's different — small inaccuracies in model labels can happen in the transcripts, sorry if i mumble model names.
[09:34] Tom: understood. do you support CPU fallbacks for light workloads?
[09:39] Jonah: partial — we discourage CPU for production low-latency but for cheap inference workloads you can run CPU in non-critical flows.
[09:46] Rajiv: data retention and logs — how long are logs kept? can partners configure retention?
[09:53] Jonah: retention is configurable per-account; we also provide token-level cost/latency breakdowns and can export to S3 for long-term retention.
[10:03] Lena: good. curious about billing integration — do you provide invoicing and partner settlement reports?
[10:10] Nina: yes we have partner billing options and settlement reports for reseller partners.
[10:16] Rajiv: what's the best next step timeline? we'd like a tech deep-dive next week and security pack sooner.
[10:23] Nina: next steps: we will send the partner one-pager and pricing by Friday (2026-03-05), Jonah to schedule tech deep-dive with Tom for 2026-03-10, and we'll send security/compliance docs by 2026-03-06.
[10:36] Tom: i'll prep a short topology doc and target workloads to share before the deep-dive.
[10:42] Jonah: great — i'll also draft a benchmarking plan (models, metrics, instance types).
[10:48] Rajiv: any blockers on your side for collaboration?
[10:52] Nina: internal enablement and resource allocation — we will prioritize pilot support if Cumulus signs for a pilot.
[10:58] Marta: one more question — do you have a partner portal for tracking leads and enablement assets?
[11:05] Nina: yes we have a partner portal, we'll invite you.
[11:10] Rajiv: perfect. thank you everyone.
[11:13] Nina: thanks all. final recap — we'll send partner deck + pricing (Nina), security pack (Jonah), schedule tech deep-dive (Jonah + Tom). action items captured. any final Qs?
[11:28] Lena: none from me.
[11:30] Rajiv: none.
[11:32] Nina: awesome — i'll follow up with calendar invites and docs. thanks!
[11:40] (call ends)
